Rufus
ROO-fus
proper noun
From the Latin Rufus, “red” or “red-haired,” a very common name among the Romans.

See also: Rufus

📖 Biblical Definition

Rufus is a believer at Rome greeted by Paul with a singular tenderness: “Salute Rufus chosen in the Lord, and his mother and mine” (Rom 16:13). Two things are said of him. He is “chosen in the Lord,” a phrase that lifts the veil upon the doctrine of election, marking Rufus as one of those whom God set His love upon and chose in Christ before the foundation of the world. And his mother had been as a mother to Paul; the apostle, who counted himself debtor to no earthly comfort, gratefully owns that this woman had shown him a mother’s kindness, and so calls her “his mother and mine.” An ancient and not unlikely tradition identifies this Rufus with the Rufus named by Mark, son of Simon the Cyrenian who bore the cross of Christ: “the father of Alexander and Rufus” (Mar 15:21). Mark, writing (as held) for the Roman church, names the sons as men known to his readers, which fits a Rufus dwelling at Rome. If so, the son of the cross-bearer became a chosen vessel, and the household that touched the Saviour’s passion was gathered into His church. Yet Scripture does not press the link, and neither will we. What is certain is enough: Rufus was chosen in the Lord, and his mother was a mother in Israel whose kindness the great apostle did not forget.

📜 Webster 1828 Definition

A believer at Rome, “chosen in the Lord,” whose mother had been a mother to Paul; perhaps the son of Simon of Cyrene.

expand to see more

RUFUS, a Christian at Rome saluted by the apostle Paul.

Called “chosen in the Lord,” a token of God’s electing grace (Rom 16:13).

His mother had shown Paul a mother’s kindness, “his mother and mine.”

His Latin name signifies “red” or “red-haired.”

Perhaps the Rufus, son of Simon the Cyrenian, named by Mark (Mar 15:21).

📖 Key Scripture

Rom 16:13 — "Salute Rufus chosen in the Lord, and his mother and mine."

Mar 15:21 — "And they compel one Simon a Cyrenian, who passed by, coming out of the country, the father of Alexander and Rufus, to bear his cross."

Eph 1:4 — "According as he hath chosen us in him before the foundation of the world, that we should be holy and without blame before him in love:"

1Th 1:4 — "Knowing, brethren beloved, your election of God."

⚠️ Modern Corruption

A saint marked “chosen in the Lord,” and the honoured kindness of a mother in Israel.

expand to see more

This entry faces no significant postmodern redefinition. The lesson to recover from Rufus is the sweetness of electing grace brought down to a single named man. To be “chosen in the Lord” is the ground of all a believer’s blessedness, and Paul greets Rufus by that very title.

The greeting honours also a mother’s love. She who mothered Paul stands for the unnumbered women whose quiet kindness sustains the servants of Christ. The household perhaps touched by the cross-bearing of Simon was gathered into the church; and whether or not the link holds, the certainty remains, that God chooses His own and binds them in families of faith and labours of love.

🔗 Greek & Hebrew Roots

A common Latin name meaning “red,” borne by a chosen saint of the Roman church.

expand to see more

Rufus — Latin, “red” or “red-haired.”

One of the commonest personal names in the Roman world.

Greeted as “chosen in the Lord” in Romans 16:13.

Possibly the son of Simon of Cyrene named in Mark 15:21.

His mother is honoured by Paul as “his mother and mine.”

Usage

"Paul saluted Rufus, chosen in the Lord, and his mother also."

"The Rufus of Romans may be the son of Simon who bore the cross."

"Rufus is greeted as one of God’s elect in the church at Rome."
